claim_tested: Writing to the GPU's GP0 command/data port (0x1F801810) via GdbClient.write_memory produces an observable change in VRAM/display content.
method: Paused via GdbClient.interrupt() at a confirmed-real-content frame, screenshotted, issued a standard GP0(A0h) CPU-to-VRAM copy-rectangle command sequence (command word, dest coord (20,20), size 16x16, 128 solid-white data words), screenshotted again immediately, CPU still paused throughout.
result: sony_before.png and sony_after.png are byte-identical (verified by hashing the actual files, not by eye). A second, earlier attempt (vram_baseline.png / vram_after_write.png, against an all-black early-boot frame) was also byte-identical.
self_correction: An earlier pass at this same experiment initially concluded the opposite (that the write caused visible framebuffer corruption), based on eyeballing dissimilar screenshots taken across a longer before-write/after-write/resume/wait sequence. A hash comparison caught that the 'before' and 'after' shots taken immediately around the write were themselves already identical -- the visual difference in the earlier, wrongly-interpreted sequence came from ordinary game rendering that happened during the resume-and-wait gap, not from the write. This was corrected before being committed anywhere.
conclusion: No evidence that this write path has any effect. Consistent with the already-documented finding that GDB writes to the 0x1F801xxx MMIO range don't reliably reach real hardware-emulation side effects (previously shown for SPU registers), now also checked for the GPU GP0 port specifically.

screenshots.check_content.png: confirmed real content (Sony logo) shortly before the second test, for context
screenshots.sony_before.png / sony_after.png: second test, paused on a frame known to reflect real display content, byte-identical

open_question: Whether GDB-issued writes to this address are dispatched to the GPU core at all in PCSX-Redux's own implementation, versus landing in a plain memory buffer with no listener -- not investigated via source reading in this pass.
